meta.semantics: BYTE-MATCH signature/member/ownership facts. A function whose mechanical C++ translation compiles to bytes IDENTICAL to the original binary (diffasm MATCH) is a closing witness for the codegen-visible parts of its declared types. Only audit-era clean records are admitted (ledger OK + clean + rule_violations==0 + this_as_id==false, and the source part_report row itself re-checks MATCH/clean/0 violations). 161B-class overfits (this-as-id) are gated out. Types must be spelled in the solver universe; rows already covered by another family are deduped; rows disjoint with another family are excluded (conflict ledger below). bm-sig: emitted signature types of the byte-identical unit (orig_size>=5; param must be used in the body). bm-member: declared type of this->NAME in the unit own hpp, emitted as the IG granularity family (plain mov pins width, not signedness). bm-owner: emitted class of a class-scoped definition (cls_src=name_prefix excluded). Vocabulary note: `int*` is unreachable through the loader (`type_universe` spells `int *`, loader normalization yields `int*` which is absent from the name table) -> 29 such rows are not emitted (counted in gate.vocab_unreachable_dropped).
